precepts.text: For thy waste and thy desolate places, and the land of thy destruction. We got destroyed. Shall even now be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants. So the land of Israel, whose capital is Jerusalem, it is not going to be enough to hold all twelve tribes. And they that swallowed thee up shall be far away. Give place to me that I may dwell. Give me enough room so that we can all live.
precepts.point: Spare not, lengthen thy cords. So when you have a tabernacle or a tent, you have cords to hold it up. And strengthen thy stakes. You use stakes to keep the tent from falling down.

note.label: The Waters of Noah Will Be Fire

precepts.why:
“Sing, O barren, thou that didst not bear”: that is our foremother Sarah, the wife of Abraham. She was desolate and could not have children, yet “more are the children of the desolate than the children of the married wife”, Hagar, the mother of Ishmael. Israel numbers as the sand of the sea; we outnumber all nations on this planet. Then Isaiah says, “Enlarge the place of thy tent.” Why? Isaiah 49 shows it.

“For thy waste and thy desolate places, and the land of thy destruction”: we got destroyed. “shall even now be too narrow by reason of the inhabitants.” The land of Israel, whose capital is Jerusalem, is not going to be enough to hold all twelve tribes. “and they that swallowed thee up shall be far away.”

“The children which thou shalt have, after thou hast lost the other”: after the two thirds that were destroyed. They “shall say again in thine ears, The place is too strait for me”: it is too narrow for us. “give place to me that I may dwell”: give us enough room so that we can all live.

That is why the tent has to be enlarged. Isaiah gives the analogy of a tent, a tabernacle, where we will dwell in Jerusalem: “let them stretch forth the curtains of thine habitations: spare not, lengthen thy cords, and strengthen thy stakes.” The cords hold the tent up and the stakes keep it from falling down. So many children are coming home that the land of our destruction will be too narrow, and we will “break forth on the right hand and on the left.”

And when they say we are thirteen percent of the population, that is propaganda. They may be counting only American blacks, but they are not counting the Jamaicans, Haitians, Puerto Ricans or Mexicans.

precepts.text: How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard? and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent? as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace, and bring glad tidings of good things! A lot of times we as the prophets do not understand the magnitude of our calling, what we have been called to do. The Lord said he would send us as saviours, and our people's salvation will come no other way but by the prophets, by the saviours that God sent, and through his word. There is no way for the people to be saved unless the saviours are sent.
precepts.point: And he said, It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth. Our job is to raise up the tribes and restore the preserved of Israel. A light to the Gentiles: that is the scattered Israelites. That thou mayest be my salvation: that you may be a saviour.

note.label: Give Diligence

precepts.why:
Isaiah says the Lord formed his servant from the womb “to bring Jacob again to him”, “to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel”, “that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.” That you may be a saviour. A lot of times we, the prophets, don’t understand the magnitude of our calling. The Lord said he would send us as saviours, and our people’s salvation will come no other way than by the prophets, the saviours God sent, and through his word. Paul shows why.

“How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? and how shall they believe in him of whom they have not heard?” This shows the importance of the prophets, the saviours: there is no way for the people to be saved unless the saviours are sent. “and how shall they hear without a preacher? And how shall they preach, except they be sent?”

We have been sent, throughout the four corners of the earth, and from the beginning, to be saviours. By going forth and teaching God’s word, salvation comes here on earth. “as it is written, How beautiful are the feet of them that preach the gospel of peace.”

That is why the prophets of God are “glorious in the eyes of the Lord.” There is no higher calling than being a prophet of the Most High God, once he has revealed his son in you at the appointed time. Some of us used to be athletes, and once Christ was awakened in us we let all that go. None of it compares to what we do now in these last days as watchmen of Israel. This is the true glory, glorious not to man but to God, and our God is our strength to raise up the tribes of Jacob.

precepts.text: For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe. Our people may see what we do as foolishness. But God says it pleased him by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe. That is our purpose. To be sent to preach God's word, to save the believers, to save the elect. And you have to take pride in it.
precepts.point: And he said, It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth. Our job is to raise up the tribes and restore the preserved of Israel. A light to the Gentiles: that is the scattered Israelites. That thou mayest be my salvation: that you may be a saviour.

note.label: Give Diligence

precepts.why:
Romans 10 asks, how shall they hear except they be sent? We have been sent to the four corners of the earth, sent from the beginning to be saviours, to “raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel.” And Paul shows the way God chose to do it: “For after that in the wisdom of God the world by wisdom knew not God, it pleased God by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.”

Our people may see what we do as foolishness. Someone may say, I’ve just been called to do this to fold. No. God says it pleased him by the foolishness of preaching to save them that believe.

That is our purpose. Preach God’s word. To be sent to preach God’s word, to save the believers, to save the elect. That is our goal and our mission, and you have to take pride in it.

So when Isaiah says the servant shall be “my salvation unto the end of the earth”, this is how: not by the wisdom of the world, which never knew God, but by the preaching of the prophets whom God formed from the womb and sent. Standing on the corner looking like a fool preaching his word is exactly what pleases him, and it is how Jacob is brought again to him.

precepts.text: Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet. That is the bowing down.
precepts.point: We can hardly fathom these words right now. Who is going to bow down before Israel? People will say you are dreaming. But guess what? That is what the scripture says. Let God be true, and every man a liar.

note.label: Why They Hated US: Walking in the Footsteps of the Persecuted

precepts.why:
Isaiah says the kings and queens of the nations “shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet.” Christ says the same thing in Revelation: “Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet.”

Those that say they are Jews and are not, but do lie, will be made to come and worship before the feet of the true Israel. That is the bowing down. Before thy feet in Revelation is with their face toward the earth, licking up the dust of thy feet, in Isaiah. The two scriptures say the same thing.

We can hardly fathom these words right now. Who is going to bow down in front of the black man? People will look at it and say you are dreaming. But guess what? That is what the scripture says. Let God be true, and every man a liar.

So don’t worry about the hatred, and don’t worry about what we are going through here. Christ is coming to save us from the hand of all that hate us, and what we have coming is greater: the Lord lifts up his hand to the Gentiles, they bring Israel’s sons in their arms and carry her daughters upon their shoulders, and “thou shalt know that I am the Lord: for they shall not be ashamed that wait for me.”

It is a light thing to raise up the tribes of Jacob and restore the preserved of Israel, the least you can do after the Lord sacrificed himself for you, and a light to the Gentiles as in Matthew 4.
precepts.point: It is two parts: the leader invites, and you accept. They straightway left their nets. Brothers sit in a chair while MOV, security, and kitchen call for help; you have followed every stat on league pass for thirteen years but do not know what the light is. Accept the invitation and at least show up to practice.

note.label: Mindset Of A Leader, Actions Of A King

precepts.why:
This is our job. “And now, saith the Lord that formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob again to him”. You were made to be the servant of God. You were made to do this work. You were not born to be a basketball player or a rapper. You were born to be a servant of God; that is our duty and our calling. “To bring Jacob again to him”: that is your commission.

“Though Israel be not gathered, yet shall I be glorious in the eyes of the Lord, and my God shall be my strength.”

“And he said, It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel”. Think about that: it is a light thing. It is the least you can do. The Lord sacrificed himself for you; our God came down and walked with us. It is a light thing to do the work of the Lord and go wake up your people.

“I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.” That is the same thing read in Matthew 4: Galilee of the Gentiles, the people that sat in darkness, saw great light. It is talking about Israel; we are to go to our brothers of the Northern Kingdom and be the light to the Gentiles, carrying on the mission God gave us.

It is a light thing to raise up the tribes of Jacob; I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles. In an acceptable time have I heard thee and in a day of salvation have I helped thee. We go to stiff-necked people who refuse to hear, but we still proclaim it.

note.label: Much Is Given, Much Is Required

precepts.why:
Isaiah 61 says to “proclaim the acceptable year of the Lord”, and Isaiah 49 says it again: “Thus saith the Lord, In an acceptable time have I heard thee, and in a day of salvation have I helped thee: and I will preserve thee, and give thee for a covenant of the people, to establish the earth, to cause to inherit the desolate heritages.” The acceptable year and the acceptable time: that is when we heal the broken heart and proclaim liberty to the captives.

“The Lord hath called me from the womb; from the bowels of my mother hath he made mention of my name. And he hath made my mouth like a sharp sword; in the shadow of his hand hath he hid me, and made me a polished shaft; in his quiver hath he hid me; And said unto me, Thou art my servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified.” We are supposed to glorify our God in this body.

“Then I said, I have laboured in vain, I have spent my strength for nought, and in vain: yet surely my judgment is with the Lord, and my work with my God.” We go to stiff-necked, hard-hearted people who refuse to hear the word of God, but we still proclaim the day of the Lord to heal those minds and tell them there is an end to this: we will rule one day. He formed us from the womb “to bring Jacob again to him.”

“It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel.” It may not appear that we are doing it, but when the numbers come in, it is a light thing he has given us, and he still charges us to raise up the children of Israel. “I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth”: that goes back to Matthew 4, the Gentiles of Galilee. Our job is to bring salvation to the people and lead them back to him, and that is a great ministry.

“Kings shall see and arise, princes also shall worship” … “and he shall choose thee.” Out of all of them, he is going to choose us. And unto whomsoever much is given, of him shall be much required: we want to be the faithful servant the Lord finds doing this work in sincerity, without deceit and without secret sins.

precepts.text: The nations lick up the dust, showing the low estate spoken to the serpent.
precepts.point: Going on the belly and eating dust means the serpent was brought to a very low estate, made like a vagabond upon the earth. Cain became a vagabond upon the earth, and so did Esau.

note.label: Genesis 3: The Craftiness of Your Enemy

precepts.why:
“And kings shall be thy nursing fathers, and their queens thy nursing mothers: they shall bow down to thee with their face toward the earth, and lick up the dust of thy feet”. The kings and queens of the nations are brought down to lick the dust at Israel's feet: a very low estate.

That is the estate spoken to the serpent: “upon thy belly shalt thou go, and dust shalt thou eat all the days of thy life”. Going on the belly and eating dust means being brought very low, made like a vagabond upon the earth. Cain became a vagabond upon the earth, and so did Esau.

precepts.text: The servant formed from the womb to bring Jacob again to the Lord is glorious in the eyes of the Lord; gathering Israel back is the highest honor on earth.
precepts.point: Rich, poor, or middle class, none of it matters to the Most High; what man holds in high esteem, God calls abomination. The highest calling anyone can have on the face of the earth is to teach the word of God and compel the lost sheep of the house of Israel to come in, so do not think less of yourself because your name carries no prestige.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
“And now, saith the Lord that formed me from the womb to be his servant, to bring Jacob again to him, Though Israel be not gathered, yet shall I be glorious in the eyes of the Lord, and my God shall be my strength.”

The servant formed from the womb to bring Jacob again to the Lord is glorious in the eyes of the Lord. Gathering Israel back is the highest honor on earth. Gideon was sent to save Israel from the hand of the Midianites and thought himself too poor and too small for it; but to be sent by the Lord for Israel is glory in his eyes, whatever man thinks of your family.

precepts.text: Thou art My servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified; the servant of this Bible is the Israelites, the ones who will get the understanding and the testimonies.
precepts.point: Therefore I love Thy commandments above gold, yea, above fine gold. Therefore I esteem all Thy precepts concerning all things to be right, and I hate every false way. You have to esteem all the laws of the Most High above everything and hate every falsehood.

note.label: Psalm 119: Blessed Are the Undefiled in the Way

precepts.why:
“I am thy servant; give me understanding, that I may know thy testimonies.” Isaiah names the servant: “Thou art my servant, O Israel, in whom I will be glorified.”

The servant of this Bible is the Israelites. They are the ones who will get the understanding and the testimonies, who love his commandments above fine gold, esteem all his precepts concerning all things to be right and hate every false way. It is time for the Most High to work, for they have made void his law, and he will be glorified in his servant Israel.

note.label: Acts 10: Cornelius and the Northern Kingdom Grafted In

“It is a light thing that thou shouldest be my servant to raise up the tribes of Jacob, and to restore the preserved of Israel: I will also give thee for a light to the Gentiles, that thou mayest be my salvation unto the end of the earth.”

The Gentiles here are the northern kingdom, the outcasts of Israel that Christ came to be a light to. That is why he spoke openly to the woman of Samaria, and why Peter was sent to Cornelius.
